page: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is an entry-tier virtual server belonging to the Cost Optimized server family. It is driven by the Arm64 architecture utilizing an Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The virtual machine provisioned via QEMU provides 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, paired with 8.0 GB of memory (roughly 1.95 GB per core). It includes 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates without an attached GPU. No complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance.

Benchmark results place the cax21 primarily in the lower tiers for compute-heavy and burst operations, reflecting its shared-core configuration and entry-level Arm core profile. The Geekbench single-core score of 1040.0 and multi-core score of 3419.0 fall into the lower quartile, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 3111.81. Extended compute routines, such as software compilation with Clang (4363.0) and PassMark physics testing (572.47), also reflect bottom-quartile throughput. In contrast, general multi-core stress-ng CPU tests reached 7055.54 and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth registered at 45.11 GB/sec, placing both metrics within the average range.

Data manipulation and I/O workloads demonstrate functional entry-level capacity. PassMark database operations scored 2684.51 (average tier), while Redis SET operations reached 4.44 million operations per second. However, cryptographic performance on the PassMark encryption test scored 637.38, falling in the bottom decile despite hardware AES support. Similarly, small LLM prompt processing (135M model) attained 169.73 tokens per second, also in the bottom decile. Storage is supported by an 80 GB NVMe SSD, but network traffic is constrained by the absence of an included IPv4 address by default.

The cax21 represents an economical resource-dense choice for budget-conscious, horizontally scalable tasks that do not require x86 instructions or high single-thread frequencies. It is appropriate for lightweight web serving, development or testing environments, entry-level database instances, and general continuous integration runners targeting the Arm64 ecosystem.
